item.title: Daily Briefing — 2026-07-16
item.description: BJJ: Crevar brings 20-match sub streak into Inner Circle 22 TONIGHT vs. Clymer in Bangkok; Musumeci-Mitchell still homeless at 8 weeks; UFC BJJ 2 July 31. Soccer: Argentina stun England 2-1 in last-minute comeback; Spain vs. Argentina Final July 19 MetLife 3pm ET; Alvarez prefers Barca but Arsenal most likely. Finance: AAPL $327.50 ATH; SPOT earnings July 20; VTI near record. NJ: Morimoto reservations live NOW on Resy; World Cup Final watch options; Shrek the Musical opens Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • ONE Inner Circle 22 TONIGHT: Helena Crevar Brings 20-Match Submission Streak vs. Paige Ivette Clymer in Bangkok
    Women's world #1 pound-for-pound Helena Crevar (355-7, 315 submission wins, 20 consecutive finishes) takes on ADCC West Coast Trials winner Paige Ivette Clymer in a 10-minute openweight grappling match at Lumpinee Stadium tonight — her final competitive appearance before ADCC Krakow September 12–13.
    Source: Combat Press
  • Musumeci-Mitchell Grappling Match Still Homeless at 8 Weeks — Both Committed, No Promotion Has Stepped Up
    Nearly two months after Bryce Mitchell challenged Mikey Musumeci and the flyweight champion publicly accepted, no organization has agreed to host the crossover grappling bout; both fighters remain publicly committed, but the match is stuck in limbo with the ADCC Krakow prep calendar filling up around them.
    Source: Low Kick MMA
  • UFC BJJ 2 Confirmed July 31: Champion Andrew Tackett Defends Against Renato Canuto in Growing No-Gi Series
    UFC's no-gi grappling series returns July 31 with champion Andrew Tackett putting his belt on the line against Brazilian submission grappling veteran Renato Canuto — the second event in a planned 14-card 2026 schedule that's rapidly positioning itself alongside ADCC and Polaris as a major destination for elite grapplers.
    Source: MMA Mania

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Argentina Stun England 2-1 With Late Comeback — Messi Assists Both Goals, Final is Spain vs. Argentina July 19 at MetLife
    Lionel Messi assisted both goals as Argentina overturned a 1-0 deficit in the final seven minutes — Enzo Fernandez's 85th-minute strike and Lautaro Martinez's 92nd-minute header — to set up a World Cup Final against Spain at MetLife Stadium on July 19, in what may be Messi's last World Cup match.
    Source: NPR
  • World Cup Final Preview: Spain (1 Goal Conceded) vs. Argentina at MetLife July 19 — Yamal vs. Messi Is the Dream Subplot
    Spain — who conceded just once in seven games — are slight favorites over defending champions Argentina in Sunday's 3pm ET final at MetLife Stadium; Lamine Yamal, who publicly dreamed of facing Messi in a final, gets his wish, while Messi's record 21 World Cup goals and Argentina's late-game resilience make the outcome far from certain.
    Source: Yahoo Sports
  • Álvarez Wants Barcelona but Atlético Won't Sell to LaLiga Rivals — Arsenal Now the Most Realistic Destination
    With Argentina's World Cup over, the Álvarez transfer crystallized: the striker prefers Barcelona but Atlético categorically refuses to sell to a domestic rival, making Arsenal — who are pushing to finalize a deal before pre-season begins next week — the most realistic path despite Álvarez's reluctance to move to England.
    Source: Football Transfers

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • AAPL Hits 15th 2026 ATH at $327.50, Up 20% YTD — Analysts Say $340 Makes Apple Second $5T Company After Nvidia
    Apple shares closed Wednesday at a new all-time high of $327.50 — up 20% year-to-date and the 15th record close of 2026 — with the market cap approaching $5 trillion; analysts say a move to ~$340 (less than 4% away) would make Apple only the second company after Nvidia to cross the $5T threshold, with July 30 Q3 earnings as the next major catalyst.
    Source: The Motley Fool
  • Spotify Q2 Earnings Expected Monday July 20 Before Open — EPS $3.29 Target, SPOT Near $480
    Multiple financial calendars point to Monday July 20 as Spotify's Q2 earnings date (before market open), with consensus expecting EPS of $3.29 — a 785% year-over-year jump — alongside updates on AI remixing features and monthly active user trajectory; SPOT trades near $480, recovering from year-to-date lows, with the analyst consensus target at $678 (~41% upside).
    Source: Earnings Whispers
  • VTI Tracks Near 52-Week High $374.70 on AAPL-Led Rally; NJ 30-Year Refinance Holds at 6.65%
    The Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF trades near its 52-week high of $374.70 as Apple's record week lifts the full market alongside continued broad breadth; New Jersey's 30-year fixed refinance rate holds at approximately 6.65% (15-year: 5.86%), keeping a refinance window open for the 52% of NJ homeowners who are equity-rich.
    Source: Bankrate

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • MM by Morimoto Reservations Now Live on Resy — Book Immediately for Iron Chef's Montclair Opening July 31
    Reservations for MM by Morimoto at 193 Glenridge Ave opened today on Resy for the July 31 dinner launch — the 12,779-sq-ft Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto concept features A5 Wagyu, an omakase bar, and premium fish flown from Japan; book now as Montclair's most anticipated 2026 restaurant opening is expected to fill within hours.
    Source: The Montclair Girl
  • World Cup Final Sunday at MetLife 3pm ET — Free Watch Options: Newark Fan Village, American Dream, NJ Transit Guide
    Sunday's World Cup Final (Spain vs. Argentina, 3pm ET on Fox) is 12 miles from Montclair at MetLife Stadium; for fans without tickets ($8,000+), free options include the Newark Fan Village (Ferry Street, Ironbound district, large screen, food hall) and the American Dream Fan Fest across from MetLife — NJ Transit runs enhanced Meadowlands trains from Penn Station from 11:30am every 15–20 minutes.
    Source: NJ Family
  • Shrek: The Musical Opens This Friday July 17 at Algonquin Arts Theatre in Manasquan — Runs Through July 26
    The Algonquin Arts Theatre in Manasquan launches Shrek: The Musical this Friday July 17 through July 26 — the fast-paced, laugh-out-loud Broadway adaptation is a great family outing about 45 minutes from Montclair, pairing well with a Jersey Shore beach day or World Cup Final watch plans this weekend.
    Source: WJRZ

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • ONE Inner Circle 22 Friday: Crevar vs. Clymer Is a Keenan-vs-Danaher Coaching Clash Nine Weeks Before ADCC
    ONE Championship has published a full profile of debutant Paige Ivette Clymer, describing her as a relentless Legion AJJ pressure passer trained by Keenan Cornelius — setting up a philosophically fascinating Keenan vs. Danaher coaching matchup against Helena Crevar nine weeks before both women compete at ADCC Krakow.
    Source: ONE Championship
  • ADCC Krakow Ticket Sales Near 4 Per Day; Duarte-Simoes Superfight Is Now the Event's Clear Top Billing
    With three defending champions absent, the Ruotolo twins out, and Gordon Ryan retired, the 15,030-seat Tauron Arena Kraków remains far from sold out ahead of September's Worlds; the Kaynan Duarte vs. Yuri Simoes openweight superfight and 14-year-old Joslyn Molina's -65kg appearance are the event's most compelling drawing cards.
    Source: BJJ World
  • Jacob Rodriguez Returns to Competition July 24 After 17-Month Hiatus at Pit Submission Series
    Former ADCC silver medalist Jacob Rodriguez will end a 17-month absence from professional grappling on July 24 at the Pit Submission Series — a notable return arriving just seven weeks before ADCC Krakow.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Spain 2-0 France: Yamal Draw Earns Penalty, Porro Finishes — La Roja in First World Cup Final Since 2010
    Lamine Yamal drew a Digne foul for Oyarzabal's 22nd-minute penalty, then Pedro Porro added a 58th-minute strike as Spain dominated France 2-0 at AT&T Stadium on Monday — sending La Roja to the July 19 MetLife Final for the first time since 2010 and ending Mbappé's tournament without a showpiece.
    Source: NBC News
  • England vs. Argentina SF Today 3pm ET in Atlanta: Messi's 21 World Cup Goals vs. Kane — MetLife Spot on the Line
    The second 2026 World Cup semifinal kicks off today (3pm ET on Fox) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, with Lionel Messi — sole holder of the all-time World Cup goals record at 21 — leading Argentina against Harry Kane and England, who seek their first Final since 1966.
    Source: ESPN
  • Atlético Transfer Desk: Arsenal Enters Álvarez Race — Formal Talks Expected This Week as Argentina's WC Run Ends Today
    The Hard Tackle reports Atlético Madrid is open to selling Julián Álvarez to Arsenal, adding the Premier League club as a third suitor alongside Barcelona and PSG; with Argentina's World Cup run ending today, formal talks are expected imminently with fee targets in the €130–150M range.
    Source: The Hard Tackle

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • VTI Near $372 Midweek as Warsh Enters Day 2 of Fed Testimony; July 30 Apple Earnings Now Top Market Catalyst
    VTI holds near $372 — close to its 52-week high of $374.70 — as new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh enters day two of his inaugural congressional testimony; with June CPI digested and bank earnings mostly in, Apple's July 30 Q3 print is now the single most closely-watched market catalyst.
    Source: Tickeron
  • AAPL 15 Days to Earnings: Near ATH at $317, China iPhone Shipments Up 20-25%; Analysts Target $1.88 EPS
    Apple shares trade near $317 — modestly below last week's all-time high of $323.45 — with analysts projecting $1.88 EPS (up ~20% YoY) on ~$108.9B revenue for the July 30 Q3 report; iPhone China shipments up 20-25% in Q2 add a positive pre-earnings signal.
    Source: MarketBeat
  • NJ 30-Year Refinance Rate Ticks to 6.66% — Still a Viable Window for Homeowners Who Locked In Near 2023's 8% Peak
    New Jersey's 30-year fixed refinance rate edged to 6.66% (15-year: 5.86%) as of July 14; homeowners who financed near the 2023 peak of ~8% still have a meaningful rate-reduction window, though economists caution a hawkish Fed September pivot could push rates higher.
    Source: Bankrate

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Act Now: MM by Morimoto Reservations Open TOMORROW on Resy — Montclair's Most Anticipated Restaurant Opening of 2026
    Reservations for MM by Morimoto open on Resy tomorrow (July 16), two weeks before the July 31 dinner launch at 193 Glenridge Ave, Montclair — the 200-seat Japanese steakhouse from Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto features A5 Wagyu, omakase bar, and tuna pizza and is expected to be one of North Jersey's most in-demand tables.
    Source: Jersey Digs
  • Final Weekend: Free Outdoor 'Much Ado About Nothing' at Van Vleck House & Gardens Through Saturday July 18
    The Studio Players' outdoor Shakespeare production runs through this Saturday July 18 at Van Vleck House & Gardens in Montclair — free admission, no tickets required, a perfect family evening before World Cup Final weekend.
    Source: Experience Montclair
  • Seussical Jr. at UCPAC July 17-19 — Family Musical This Weekend in Cranford, 20 Minutes From Montclair
    CAU Community Players bring Seussical Jr. to the Union County Performing Arts Center in Cranford this Friday through Sunday (July 17-19) — the beloved Dr. Seuss mashup featuring Cat in the Hat and Horton, a great family theater option about 20 minutes from Montclair.
    Source: NJ Stage

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • ONE: The Inner Circle July 17 Preview — Ruotolo Fights Tetsuka in MMA; Crevar vs. Clymer in Grappling
    Thursday's ONE: The Inner Circle card at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok features Kade Ruotolo facing Hiroyuki Tetsuka in an MMA clash alongside women's grappling #1 Helena Crevar battling ADCC West Coast Trials winner Paige Ivette Clymer in a submission grappling match.
    Source: SportsKeeda
  • Joslyn Molina, 14, Confirmed as Youngest-Ever ADCC Worlds Competitor for Krakow September 12–13
    Joslyn Molina has officially accepted her invitation to the -65kg division at ADCC 2026 in Krakow, making her the youngest competitor in ADCC history; ADCC amended its minimum-age policy after Molina won bronze at the East Coast Trials competing against adult opponents.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • World Cup SF Today: France vs. Spain at AT&T Stadium Dallas (3pm ET) — Winner to MetLife Final July 19
    The first 2026 World Cup semifinal kicks off this afternoon with Kylian Mbappé (7 goals) leading France against Lamine Yamal and Spain; the winner earns a spot in Saturday's Final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ — now five days away.
    Source: ESPN
  • England vs. Argentina SF Tomorrow July 15, Atlanta (3pm ET): Kane & Bellingham vs. Messi — Final Spot at Stake
    Wednesday's second World Cup semifinal at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta has England chasing their first Final since 1966, with Kane and Bellingham each on 6 tournament goals, against Messi's Argentina (8 goals, 2022 defending champions); analysts predict a tight, low-scoring affair.
    Source: Al Jazeera
  • Álvarez Transfer Breakthrough: Apollo Sports Capital Now Backing Sale; Lamine Yamal Made Personal Request
    In the biggest shift yet in the Julián Álvarez saga, Atlético's majority shareholders Apollo Sports Capital are increasingly prepared to sanction a transfer to Barcelona, while Lamine Yamal has personally requested the club sign the striker; formal talks resume once Argentina exits the World Cup.
    Source: Football Transfers

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • June CPI Released: Headline Falls to ~3.9% on Gas Price Drop; Core Sticky at 2.85% — Warsh Testimony Begins Today
    The BLS released June CPI this morning (8:30am ET): headline inflation fell from 4.2% to approximately 3.9% YoY, driven by a ~10% drop in gasoline prices from the US-Iran ceasefire; core CPI held at ~2.85% — well above the Fed's 2% target — with new Chair Kevin Warsh beginning his inaugural congressional testimony today and the July FOMC rate decision in sharp focus.
    Source: Kiplinger
  • AAPL Hits All-Time High $323.45; Citi Raises Target to $365 Ahead of July 30 Earnings
    Apple shares set a new intraday all-time high of $323.45 on July 13 (closing at $317.31) after Citi upgraded its price target from $315 to $365, citing AI strategy momentum and continued market share gains; July 30 Q3 earnings are next, where analysts project $1.89 EPS on 14–17% revenue growth.
    Source: FX Leaders
  • Spotify Earnings Confirmed August 4 — Later Than Expected; Q1 Beat Showed 761M MAU, Analyst Consensus $678
    Spotify's next earnings date is confirmed as August 4 before market open, later than the widely-reported July 29 date; Q1 2026 delivered 761M monthly active users (+12% YoY) and $5.3B revenue (+8%), with soft Q2 guidance weighing on shares despite a $678 analyst consensus target implying ~40% upside.
    Source: Market Chameleon

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Ocean County Fair Opens Tomorrow July 15 Through July 19 — Rides, 4-H Animals, Fair Food, $10 Admission
    The five-day Ocean County Fair runs July 15–19 at Robert J. Miller Air Park in Berkeley Township (~70 miles from Montclair near Exit 88 GSP), featuring 4-H animal exhibits, carnival rides, live entertainment, and classic fair food; admission is $10 for adults, free for kids under 10.
    Source: NJ Family
  • Where to Watch the World Cup Final July 19 Near Montclair — Free Fan Zone at Liberty State Park, NJ DOT Advisory
    For fans unable to pay $8K+ for MetLife tickets, the official FIFA Fan Festival at Liberty State Park in Jersey City (free, opens 9am July 19) is about 20 minutes from Montclair; NJ DOT has issued traffic advisories for the MetLife area with heavy congestion expected around Route 3 from midday Saturday.
    Source: NJ Family
  • Two Free Movies Coming Up: Zootopia 2 at State Theatre NJ July 21; 'Best in Show' at Anderson Park July 26
    Next Tuesday July 21, State Theatre NJ in New Brunswick screens Zootopia 2 for free (10:30am and 6:30pm showings, crafts at 5:30pm); Sunday July 26, Montclair Film's 'Movie Night Under the Stars' shows 'Best in Show' free at Anderson Park with a pre-show dog parade.
    Source: State Theatre NJ

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Polaris 38: Szczecinski Wins Welterweight GP, Sarah Galvao Captures Bantamweight Title
    At Polaris 38 on July 11, Mateusz Szczecinski won the welterweight grand prix with three straight wins and a $30,000 prize; Sarah Galvao submitted Zara Di Tofano with an arm-triangle choke to claim the Polaris bantamweight championship.
    Source: Jits Magazine
  • Kade Ruotolo Returns From Injury to Defend ONE Lightweight Title This Thursday; Crevar–Clymer Also on Card
    After withdrawing injured in June, Kade Ruotolo is back to defend his ONE Lightweight Submission Grappling World Title at ONE: The Inner Circle on July 17 in Bangkok — with women's #1 P4P Helena Crevar vs. ADCC West Coast Trials winner Paige Ivette Clymer on the same card.
    Source: MMA Sucka
  • ADCC Miami Open Concluded July 11 — Last Major North American Qualifier Before Krakow Worlds
    The ADCC Miami-Dade Open wrapped Saturday July 11 at the Miami-Dade County Fair & Exposition, awarding 9 world ranking points to first-place finishers in the final major North American qualifier before September's ADCC Worlds in Krakow.
    Source: ADCC Combat

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • World Cup SFs Kick Off Tomorrow: France vs. Spain (July 14, Dallas, 3pm ET) and England vs. Argentina (July 15, Atlanta)
    The 2026 World Cup semifinals feature the first-ever bracket with FIFA's top-four ranked nations — France (1st) vs. Spain (3rd) at AT&T Stadium tomorrow at 3pm ET on Fox, and Argentina (2nd) vs. England (4th) Wednesday in Atlanta; winners meet at MetLife Stadium, NJ on July 19.
    Source: Yahoo Sports
  • World Cup Final at MetLife July 19: BTS, Shakira, Justin Bieber Halftime; Resale From $8K
    The 2026 FIFA World Cup Final comes to MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ on July 19 at 3pm ET — 12 miles from Montclair — with a halftime show featuring BTS, Shakira, and Justin Bieber; secondary market resale starts at roughly $8,000–$9,775 for upper-deck seats.
    Source: MetLife Stadium
  • Sørloth Exit From Atlético Expected After Norway's QF Loss — Juventus Deal Nears Completion
    Alexander Sørloth's Norway fell 2-1 to England in the quarterfinals on July 11 (Bellingham brace), ending his World Cup; the result clears the way for his Juventus transfer — the clubs remain ~€5M apart on a fee of ~€30–35M, with a deal expected imminently.
    Source: Into the Calderon
  • Álvarez Transfer on Hold Until Argentina's World Cup Run Ends; Barcelona Readying Post-Tournament Bid
    With Julián Álvarez still competing with Argentina (SF vs. England, July 15), Barcelona has paused formal transfer negotiations until the World Cup concludes; the club is expected to submit a revised bid close to €130M after Argentina's exit or the final.
    Source: Football Transfers

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Big Week: June CPI Tuesday, Fed Chair Warsh Inaugural Testimony, Q2 Earnings Season Kicks Off
    Markets face a critical week with June CPI data Tuesday (consensus +3.8% YoY, down from May's 4.2%), new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's inaugural congressional testimony Tuesday–Wednesday, and Q2 earnings season launching with JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BofA, Netflix, and TSMC all reporting.
    Source: CNBC
  • Apple Sues OpenAI for AI Hardware Trade Secret Theft — AAPL at $315, July 30 Earnings Next
    Apple filed a landmark lawsuit against OpenAI on July 10, alleging former Apple execs at Jony Ive's io Products directed job candidates to bring Apple parts and download confidential specs; AAPL closed near $315 and the July 30 fiscal Q3 earnings call is the next major catalyst.
    Source: CNBC
  • Spotify SPOT Down 38% From ATH but Consensus Target $678 — July 29 Earnings the Reset Catalyst
    Spotify shares are roughly 38% below their all-time high, but JPMorgan raised its target to $650 and Wells Fargo to $600, pushing the Street consensus to $678 (~40% upside); Q2 earnings are due July 29 before market open, with analysts watching MAU (target 778M) and gross margins (target 33%+).
    Source: Benzinga
  • NJ ANCHOR Payments Start September 15 — Up to $1,500 for Homeowners; Mortgage Rate Rises to 6.49%
    New Jersey's ANCHOR property tax relief program begins distributing 2026 payments September 15, with eligible homeowners receiving up to $1,500 ($1,750 with senior bonus); NJ's 30-year fixed mortgage rate has risen to 6.49% this week ahead of Tuesday's critical CPI data.
    Source: Kiplinger

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • World Cup Final at MetLife July 19 — Six Days Away, NJ's Biggest Sports Event in 32 Years
    The 2026 FIFA World Cup Final comes to MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford on July 19 at 3pm ET — 12 miles from Montclair — with BTS, Shakira, and Justin Bieber performing at halftime; the largest sporting event ever held in NJ and the last chance to see the World Cup in person this summer.
    Source: MetLife Stadium
  • Adventure Aquarium 'Shark & Ray Summer Adventure' Opens Today — July 13 Through August 16 in Camden
    Adventure Aquarium's Shark & Ray Summer Adventure kicks off today in Camden, featuring the Northeast's largest shark collection alongside daily marine biologist talks, hands-on ray encounters, sing-alongs, and dance parties — a family-friendly destination about 90 minutes from Montclair.
    Source: NJ Family
  • Montclair Jazz Soundcheck TOMORROW July 14: Michele Rosewoman & Quintessence at Lackawanna Station — Free
    The Montclair Jazz Festival's free outdoor Soundcheck Series continues Monday July 14 with pianist Michele Rosewoman and her acclaimed Afro-Cuban ensemble Quintessence at Lackawanna Station; free and open to all, leading to the August 15 Downtown Jamboree headlined by Dianne Reeves.
    Source: Montclair Jazz Festival
  • Car-Free Church Street Weekend Returns July 17–19 — Outdoor Dining, Shops, No Traffic
    Montclair's second pedestrian weekend of 2026 closes Church Street to vehicles from 10am–10pm July 17–19, turning the restaurant-lined block into an outdoor plaza — a great family outing near The Clairidge theater, running concurrently with the World Cup Final weekend.
    Source: Montclair Local

    The ADCC Miami-Dade Open holds weigh-ins July 10 (4–7pm) and competition July 11, with registration closing Thursday July 9; first-place finishers earn 9 ADCC world ranking points in the last major North American opportunity before September's Krakow Worlds.

    Women's world #1 P4P Helena Crevar faces ADCC West Coast Trials winner Paige Ivette Clymer in a 10-minute openweight submission match at Lumpinee Stadium on July 17 — a high-profile tune-up nine weeks before ADCC Krakow.
    Source: ONE Championship

    A week after Bryce Mitchell's callout and Mikey Musumeci's full acceptance, no organization has stepped forward to host the crossover grappling match; the bout is stuck in limbo until a promotion steps up.
    Source: Low Kick MMA

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • France vs. Morocco World Cup QF Tomorrow (July 9, 4pm ET) — Mbappé's 7 Goals vs. Unbeaten Atlas Lions
    France arrive at Gillette Stadium unbeaten in five games with 14 goals and only two conceded, with Mbappé setting a new World Cup knockout-stage scoring record at 7 goals; Morocco are equally unbeaten in a rematch of their 2022 semifinal.
    Source: FIFA
  • Spain vs. Belgium QF Friday July 10 at SoFi Stadium (3pm ET) — Five Clean Sheets vs. Tournament's Biggest Attack
    Spain reach Los Angeles with five consecutive clean sheets including a grinding 1-0 over Portugal; Belgium bring De Bruyne and Lukaku after demolishing the USMNT 4-1 — making this the quarterfinal most likely to produce an upset.
    Source: Yahoo Sports
  • Álvarez Transfer Saga Intensifies: Barcelona Sets World Cup Deadline; Atlético Cites €500M Clause
    Julián Álvarez publicly confirmed he wants out, telling reporters his departure 'is the best thing for everyone'; Barcelona set a World Cup-end deadline and will move on if no deal is struck, while Atlético insists no fee short of the €500M release clause works.
    Source: Barca Blaugranes
  • Lee Kang-in Still Awaiting Official Atlético Announcement — €40M+ Confirmed, 5-Year Deal Agreed
    Despite Fabrizio Romano's 'Here We Go' on July 7, no official announcement was posted as of July 8; Korean media confirm the fee is slightly above €40M with bonuses on a deal through 2031, making him the first Asian player in Atlético's history.
    Source: Korea JoongAng Daily

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Chip Sell-Off Resumes: Samsung Miss + DeepSeek AI News Sinks Nasdaq 1.16%, VTI Pulls Back From $372
    U.S. stocks fell Tuesday after Samsung's earnings miss and reports China's DeepSeek is developing its own AI chip triggered fresh semiconductor selling; the Nasdaq fell 1.16%, S&P 500 dropped 0.45% to 7,503, Dow lost 130 pts to 52,925, and VTI retreated from ~$372.
    Source: TheStreet
  • AAPL Dips to ~$310 as Analyst Warns Foldable iPhone Supply Issues Could Miss September Launch
    Apple stock slipped premarket Wednesday after an analyst warned supply constraints on the foldable 'iPhone Ultra' could push its launch past September 2026; AAPL closed at ~$310 Tuesday with July 30 Q3 earnings as the next major catalyst.
    Source: StockTwits
  • SPOT Up ~6% in Early July Heading Into July 29 Earnings — 34 of 40 Analysts Rate Buy
    Spotify has gained roughly 6% since July 1 as investors position for the July 29 Q2 report; consensus targets 778M MAUs, 33%+ gross margins, and EPS of ~$3.18, with BofA's $685 Buy target among a strong analyst consensus.
    Source: Yahoo Finance
  • NJ Senior Freeze Property Tax Checks Begin July 15 — ANCHOR in September; 30-Year Refinance at 6.13%
    NJ's Senior Freeze (PTR) program begins mailing 2026 property tax reimbursement checks July 15; ANCHOR benefits arrive in September and Stay NJ in February 2027 — with the 30-year fixed refinance rate at ~6.13%, down sharply from the 2023 peak near 8%.
    Source: NJ Division of Taxation

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Newark Black Film Festival Opens TONIGHT at Newark Museum of Art — Free Screening of 'When We Free the World'
    The 52nd Newark Black Film Festival launches tonight July 8 at 6:30pm with an Opening Night Reception and screening of 'When We Free the World' at the Newark Museum of Art; the free (reservation required) series runs every Wednesday through August 5, about 12 miles from Montclair.
    Source: Newark Black Film Festival
  • Montclair Jazz Soundcheck: Michele Rosewoman & Quintessence Next Monday July 14 at Lackawanna Station — Free
    The Montclair Jazz Festival's free outdoor Soundcheck Series continues with jazz pianist Michele Rosewoman and her Afro-Cuban ensemble Quintessence next Monday July 14 at Lackawanna Station; the series runs through August 4 ahead of the August 15 Downtown Jamboree.
    Source: Montclair Jazz Festival
  • State Theatre Free Movies: Lilo & Stitch Next Tuesday July 14 in New Brunswick — Two Showings, Crafts at 5:30pm
    The State Theatre NJ's free Summer Movies Series continues next Tuesday July 14 with Lilo & Stitch (10:30am and 6:30pm), with movie-themed crafts at 5:30pm before the evening showing; remaining: Zootopia 2 (July 21) and How to Train Your Dragon (July 28) — all free on a 46-foot screen in New Brunswick.
    Source: State Theatre NJ

Soccer: Spain 1-0 Portugal (Ronaldo out); Belgium 4-1 USA; QF bracket set; Lee Kang-in & Atletico "Here We Go." Finance: Dow tops 53,000; AAPL-Broadcom chip deal; BofA $685 SPOT target; NJ mortgage 6.03%. NJ: Free movies State Theatre today; VRG vintage racing NJMP July 10-12; Morimoto opens July 31.
item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Mikey Musumeci Accepts Bryce Mitchell's Grappling Challenge After 'Gay' Comment
    Bryce Mitchell publicly challenged Mikey Musumeci while saying he refuses to watch BJJ because it's "gay"; Musumeci accepted with a troll response and jokingly ruled out leg locks and guard pulling, and Mitchell confirmed the match is on — though no date or promotion has been announced yet.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe
  • ADCC 2026 Quietly Removes Izaak Michell From Krakow Roster Amid Active Arrest Warrants
    ADCC has removed Izaak Michell from its official Krakow competitor list after months of controversy — including Craig Jones withdrawing his $48k equal-pay pledge in protest — following reports Michell faces two active Texas arrest warrants related to sexual assault allegations.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe
  • ADCC 2026 in Krakow Selling Just 4 Tickets per Day at 15,000-Seat Venue
    With Gordon Ryan absent and multiple stars out, ticket sales for September's ADCC Worlds at the 15,030-seat Tauron Arena Kraków average only ~4 per day; analysts cite weak main-event appeal, steep pricing relative to Polish wages, and the Michell controversy as compounding factors.
    Source: BJJ World

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Spain 1-0 Portugal: Merino Header Ends Ronaldo's World Cup in Dallas
    Mikel Merino came off the bench to head in a stoppage-time winner at AT&T Stadium, eliminating Portugal and likely ending Cristiano Ronaldo's World Cup career at age 41; Spain advances to the quarterfinals to face Belgium on July 10 in Los Angeles.
    Source: Al Jazeera
  • Belgium 4-1 USA: De Ketelaere Brace Ends Host Nation's World Cup Dream in Seattle
    Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and set up another as Belgium dominated the USMNT 4-1, with Romelu Lukaku adding a stoppage-time fourth; Belgium meets Spain in the quarterfinals on July 10 in Los Angeles.
    Source: Yahoo Sports
  • World Cup QF Bracket Set: France-Morocco, Spain-Belgium, Norway-England Headline
    The quarterfinal schedule is confirmed: France vs. Morocco (July 9, Boston), Spain vs. Belgium (July 10, Los Angeles), Norway vs. England (July 11, Miami) — Atlético striker Alexander Sørloth and Norway are through to the final eight.
    Source: Al Jazeera
  • Romano Issues 'Here We Go' on Lee Kang-in to Atlético Madrid — Announcement Imminent
    Transfer insider Fabrizio Romano confirmed all parties agreed on a €35m plus €5m add-ons deal with a five-year contract, with Lee turning down a Middle East offer; the official club announcement is the only remaining step.
    Source: Seoul Economic Daily

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Dow Hits 53,000 for the First Time; Foxconn Beat Sparks AI Optimism, VTI Reaches ~$372
    U.S. equities opened Q3 strong Monday with the Dow closing above 53,000 for the first time, S&P 500 up 0.7%, and Nasdaq up 1.1%, driven by Foxconn's stronger-than-expected quarterly sales; VTI advanced to ~$372, near its 52-week high of $374.70.
    Source: Yahoo Finance
  • Apple and Broadcom Extend Custom Chip Partnership Through 2031; AAPL Climbs to ~$313
    Apple and Broadcom extended their chip supply deal covering custom ASICs, cellular modem components, and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth silicon; AAPL rose ~1% to ~$313 and Broadcom jumped over 3%, removing near-term supply uncertainty heading into July 30 Q3 earnings.
    Source: Yahoo Finance
  • BofA Names Spotify a Top Q3 Pick With $685 Price Target — 41% Upside Implied
    Bank of America analyst Jessica Reif Ehrlich issued a Buy call on Spotify with a $685 price target, citing a compelling product roadmap and new pricing tiers — implying ~41% upside — three weeks ahead of the July 29 earnings report.
    Source: CNBC
  • NJ 30-Year Mortgage Rate at 6.03% — Nearly 60 Basis Points Below the National Average
    New Jersey's 30-year fixed purchase rate stands at 6.03% versus the 6.61% national average as of July 6, with the 15-year fixed at 5.38%; NJ homeowners who financed near the 2023 ~8% peak have a real refinance window, though sub-4% pandemic-era mortgage holders should stay put.
    Source: Bankrate

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • State Theatre NJ Free Summer Movies Kicks Off Today With 'A Minecraft Movie' — Two Showings
    The State Theatre's free Tuesday summer series begins today in New Brunswick with A Minecraft Movie at 10:30 AM and 6:30 PM; the July lineup continues with Lilo & Stitch (July 14), Zootopia 2 (July 21), and How to Train Your Dragon (July 28) — all free, with evening shows including movie-themed arts and crafts at 5:30 PM.
    Source: BroadwayWorld NJ
  • Vintage Race Cars at NJMP This Weekend — VRG Glasstown Speedfest July 10-12 in Millville
    The Vintage Racer Group debuts at NJ Motorsports Park with a three-day event on the Lightning Circuit (July 10-12), featuring classic sports racers in nearly 3 hours of daily track time — a rare chance to watch authentic vintage road racing about 90 minutes from Montclair.
    Source: NJ Motorsports Park
  • Iron Chef Morimoto Opens MM by Morimoto in Montclair July 31 — Reservations Open July 16
    Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto is opening a nearly 13,000-sq-ft, 200-seat Japanese steakhouse at 193 Glenridge Ave featuring an omakase bar, Japanese A5 Wagyu, tuna pizza, and premium fish from Japan; reservations on Resy open July 16, two weeks before the July 31 dinner launch.
    Source: Jersey Digs

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Rosas Jr. Submits Khasan at ACBJJ 21 via RNC; Zabit Reignites Rivalry With Ringside Face-Off
    Raul Rosas Jr. captured the ACBJJ 21 All Stars Championship in Moscow on July 5, finishing short-notice replacement Khasan Magomedsharipov with a rear naked choke; after watching his brother lose, Zabit appeared ringside for a face-off with Rosas Jr., strongly signaling the original matchup is being rebooked.
    Source: Bloody Elbow
  • ADCC Miami-Dade Open This Saturday July 11 — Registration Closes Thursday, 9 Points for 1st Place
    The last major North American ADCC qualifier before September's Krakow World Championship is five days away; registration closes Thursday July 9 ($150) and first-place finishers earn 9 ADCC world ranking points — crucial currency for athletes still chasing Krakow invitations.
    Source: ADCC Combat
  • Jorge Masvidal Booked for Submission Grappling Match vs. UFC's Shara Magomedov
    Former UFC BMF champion Jorge Masvidal is scheduled to compete in a submission grappling match against rising UFC middleweight Shara "Bullet" Magomedov, the latest high-profile MMA crossover adding marquee appeal to the professional no-gi grappling circuit.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Norway Shocks Brazil 2-0 at MetLife, England Beats Mexico 3-2 at Azteca — R16 Day 2 Results
    Alexander Sørloth and Erling Haaland powered Norway to a stunning 2-0 elimination of Brazil at MetLife Stadium, while England survived a 3-2 thriller against Mexico at the Azteca; Atlético striker Sørloth is now a World Cup quarterfinal participant.
    Source: Yahoo Sports
  • Today's World Cup R16: Portugal vs. Spain at AT&T Stadium Dallas (3pm ET); USA vs. Belgium in Seattle (8pm ET)
    Two blockbuster Round of 16 clashes today: Ronaldo's Portugal faces Atlético's Alex Baena and Spain in an all-Iberian derby at AT&T Stadium, Dallas (3pm ET, FS1), followed by host USA against Belgium at Lumen Field, Seattle (8pm ET, Fox).
    Source: ESPN
  • Sørloth's Norway Stuns Brazil, Boosting Exit Value; Lee Kang-in Atlético Deal Still Awaiting Official Announcement
    Alexander Sørloth's starring World Cup run raises his price in exit talks with Juventus (~€30-35M); separately, Lee Kang-in's agreed move from PSG to Atlético (~€30M, 5-year deal) was described as "on the verge" by French Football Weekly on July 5, with the official announcement still pending.
    Source: French Football Weekly

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • AAPL Near $308 With Wedbush's $400 Target Intact; Foldable iPhone Ultra Is the H2 Bull Thesis Into July 30 Earnings
    Apple shares are holding near $308 — up roughly 7% in the holiday week — as Wedbush maintains its $400 price target built around a 10-million-unit foldable "iPhone Ultra" production ramp (~$2,500) and the new Google Cloud AI partnership; fiscal Q3 earnings July 30 are the next major catalyst.
    Source: MarketBeat
  • PSE&G Electric Bills Down 1.8% Since June 1; NJ Homeowners Can Save Additional 11% by Switching to a Competitive Supplier
    Average PSE&G residential electricity bills fell $3.23/month (about 1.8%) starting June 1 with summer credits also in effect; NJ homeowners can cut supply costs a further 11% by switching to a competitive provider at roughly 17.6 cents/kWh versus PSE&G's 19.9 cents — a meaningful saving ahead of peak summer usage.
    Source: NJ1015
  • Spotify SPOT Down 33% YTD Entering Q3 — Analysts See July 29 Earnings as Reset Catalyst
    Spotify shares enter Q3 2026 down roughly 33% year-to-date, but multiple analysts — including Bernstein (Buy, reaffirmed July 3) — view the July 29 earnings as a sentiment reset: Q2 guidance targets 778M monthly active users, 33%+ gross margins, and growing Audiobooks+ revenue that could drive a sharp re-rating if met.
    Source: MarketBeat

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Montclair Bastille Day Weekend July 11-12: French Cinema at The Clairidge, Garden Party at Van Vleck House
    L'Alliance French Institute is hosting a Bastille Day Weekend in Montclair: Martin Provost's film "Bonnard: Pierre et Marthe" screens at The Clairidge Saturday July 11 at 7pm; Sunday July 12 brings a town-wide French Shopping Day, outdoor story time at Watchung Booksellers, and a garden party at Van Vleck House & Gardens (5-9pm).
    Source: The Montclair Girl
  • Maplewoodstock Music + Arts Festival This Weekend July 11-12 — 22 Bands, 60+ Vendors, Free for All Ages
    Maplewoodstock's 21st edition arrives at Maplewood's Memorial Park (580 Valley Street) Saturday-Sunday July 11-12, noon to 9:30pm, headlined by Lettuce, Anders Osborne, and Slap Dragon; the free event features 60+ art vendors, a Kid Zone, beer garden, and food trucks — a 5-minute drive from Montclair.
    Source: The Montclair Girl
  • Montclair Flea Returns This Weekend — Saturday & Sunday July 11-12 at Lackawanna Plaza, 11am-5pm
    The Montclair Flea is back at 1 Lackawanna Plaza on Saturday and Sunday July 11-12 (11am-5pm), with curated art, vintage goods, and local food vendors — a rain-or-shine family outing that pairs well with the Summer of Soccer watch parties still running next door at Lackawanna Station.
    Source: Lackawanna Station

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • ACBJJ 21 Live Today in Moscow: Khasan Magomedsharipov Headlines vs. Raul Rosas Jr. in Short-Notice Main Event
    Zabit's younger brother Khasan takes center stage at ACBJJ 21 today in Moscow, facing UFC bantamweight contender Raul Rosas Jr. after Zabit's late injury withdrawal; Khasan enters on one week's notice after a first-round submission win at PFL San Diego.
    Source: MiddleEasy
  • ADCC Miami-Dade Open July 11: Last Major North American Qualifier Six Days Away
    The ADCC Miami-Dade Open at the Miami-Dade County Fair & Exposition on July 11 is one of the final qualifying events before September's ADCC World Championship in Krakow; weigh-ins run July 10 from 4–7pm with competition starting at 8am on the 11th.
    Source: ADCC Combat

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Morocco 3-0 Canada, France 1-0 Paraguay: World Cup R16 Day 1 Delivers African Dominance and Mbappé Ice
    Morocco demolished co-host Canada 3-0 on July 4 with Azzedine Ounahi netting a brace; France edged Paraguay 1-0 via Kylian Mbappé's converted penalty to advance to the quarterfinals for a record fourth consecutive World Cup.
    Source: CNN
  • World Cup R16 Day 2: Brazil vs. Norway at MetLife (4pm ET), Mexico vs. England at Azteca (8pm ET)
    The Round of 16 continues today with Brazil meeting Norway at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford at 4pm ET, and Mexico hosting England at the historic Estadio Azteca at 8pm ET — the first World Cup match at the Azteca since 1986.
    Source: ESPN
  • Simeone Breaks Silence on Álvarez: Future 'Will Be Resolved This Summer' as World Cup Winds Down
    Atlético coach Diego Simeone addressed the Julián Álvarez situation publicly for the first time, saying his future "will be resolved this summer" while keeping him in current plans — the clearest dugout signal yet that a departure is probable once the tournament concludes.
    Source: ESPN
  • Atlético Activates Korean Market Push as Lee Kang-in Signing Awaits Final Stamp
    With Lee Kang-in's move from PSG to Atlético all but sealed at ~€30M through 2031, the club is already building marketing partnerships targeting South Korea's football fanbase ahead of his debut as the first-ever Asian player in club history.
    Source: The Korea Herald

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Markets Reopen Monday With Dow at Record; July 6 Week: ISM Services, Fed Minutes, Chip Sector Recovery in Focus
    U.S. markets resume Monday July 6 with the Dow at an all-time record and VTI near multi-month highs; key watchpoints include ISM Services (Monday), Fed minutes (Wednesday), and whether the semiconductor selloff — Micron –7%, SanDisk –14% — stabilizes heading into Q3.
    Source: CNBC
  • Spotify (SPOT): Bernstein Reaffirms Buy; 778M MAU Target and July 29 Earnings Are the Next Inflection Point
    Bernstein maintained its Buy rating on Spotify on July 2, citing Q2 guidance of 778M monthly active users and 33%+ gross margins; the July 29 earnings call — the quarter after a 17% EPS beat in Q1 — is the key test for whether the stock's recovery accelerates into H2.
    Source: Yahoo Finance
  • VTI Posts 22.75% One-Year Total Return Through Holiday Close; Index Investors Enter Q3 on Solid Ground
    Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) closed the Independence Day holiday period with a 22.75% one-year total return including dividends, holding 3,449 stocks with $657.9B in assets — entering Q3 on solid footing even as tech-sector volatility picked up late in Q2.
    Source: StockAnalysis

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • World Cup R16 at MetLife Today: Brazil vs. Norway at 4pm ET — Holiday Weekend Soccer 12 Miles from Montclair
    The World Cup Round of 16 brings Brazil vs. Norway to MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford at 4pm ET today, just 12 miles from Montclair and accessible via NJ Transit — a natural last-minute family outing before the tournament's games shift westward.
    Source: ESPN
  • State Theatre NJ Free Summer Movies Begin Tuesday July 7 in New Brunswick — Weekly Tuesdays Through July 28
    State Theatre New Jersey in New Brunswick launches its free Summer Movies Series this Tuesday July 7, with morning and evening screenings on a 46-foot screen; the series runs July 7, 14, 21, and 28 — about 12 miles from Montclair and a great school-break option for families.
    Source: NJ Family
  • Branchburg's America 250 Celebration Today at White Oak Park: Rock Wall, Ninja Course, Live Music, Fireworks Through 9pm
    Branchburg wraps its Semiquincentennial celebration today July 5 at White Oak Park (12pm–9pm) with live music, food trucks, and a full kids zone including rock wall, bungee trampoline, ninja warrior obstacle course, and pony rides — a great final weekend outing about 35 miles from Montclair.
    Source: NJ Is Not Boring

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • ADCC 2026 Full 128-Competitor Roster Confirmed: Three Defending Champs Out, Ruotolo Twins and All UFC BJJ Champions Also Missing
    With all 128 slots confirmed for September's ADCC Worlds in Krakow, the bracket shows historic star-power gaps: defending 66kg champ Diogo Reis joins Mica Galvao and Giancarlo Bodoni among withdrawals, while neither Kade nor Tye Ruotolo, Nick Rodriguez, nor any current UFC BJJ titleholder will compete.
    Source: MMA Mania
  • ADCC Croatia Open Qualifier Live Today in Zadar; Miami-Dade Open Follows July 11
    The ADCC global qualifier roadshow reaches the Croatia Open today at Kresimir Cosic Sports Hall in Zadar, with athletes competing for Krakow spots; the Miami-Dade Open on July 11 is the next major stop before September's World Championship.
    Source: ADCC Combat
  • Kaynan Duarte vs. Yuri Simoes Superfight Gains New Weight as ADCC 2026 Field Thins
    With three defending champs and the Ruotolo twins absent, the Kaynan Duarte vs. Yuri Simoes superfight for Gordon Ryan's vacated ADCC title becomes the event's clearest marquee matchup — and the contest most likely to define the super-heavyweight division's next dominant force.
    Source: ADCC Combat

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Argentina Survive World Cup Scare, Beat Cape Verde 3–2 AET: Messi Scores as Islanders Equalize Twice
    Argentina won 3-2 in extra time on July 3 after Cape Verde equalized twice in stunning fashion; Messi and Lautaro Martinez scored, but Lopes Cabral's long-range curler forced extra time before a last-gasp Diney Borges own goal sealed Argentina's survival.
    Source: Al Jazeera
  • World Cup R16 Double-Header Today: Canada vs. Morocco in Houston (1pm ET), France vs. Paraguay in Philadelphia (5pm ET)
    The 2026 World Cup Round of 16 opens with two Independence Day games: Canada meets Morocco at NRG Stadium, Houston, and France — led by Mbappé's record six knockout-stage goals — face upset-specialists Paraguay at Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia.
    Source: Al Jazeera
  • Atlético Transfer Roundup: Lee Kang-in Announcement Imminent; Álvarez–Barcelona Deadlock Continues
    Atlético Madrid's official signing of Lee Kang-in from PSG (≈€30M, 5 years) is expected within days, making him the club's first Asian player; separately, Laporta confirmed Barcelona's €100M Álvarez bid remains on the table while Atlético holds firm at €150M with no movement during the World Cup.
    Source: Football Transfers

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • AAPL Closes at $308.63, Best Session of 2026 (+4.84%): Foldable iPhone Ultra Plans and Google Cloud AI Deal Drive Pre-Holiday Surge
    Apple surged 4.84% on July 3 — best single-day gain of 2026 — after reports targeting 10M units of a foldable "iPhone Ultra" (~$2,500) and a new Google Cloud AI partnership; Q3 earnings on July 30 are the next major catalyst.
    Source: CNBC
  • Apple in Talks to Source Chips From Two Pentagon-Blacklisted Chinese Makers (CXMT and YMTC) to Ease Global Memory Crunch
    Apple is negotiating supply agreements with CXMT and YMTC — both on the Pentagon's entity list — to ease the AI-driven memory shortage that has forced product price hikes; the strategy requires U.S. government clearance and carries bipartisan political risk.
    Source: Bloomberg
  • NJ 30-Year Mortgage Rate Edges Up to 6.36% as of July 3; Markets Closed for Independence Day with Dow at All-Time Record
    New Jersey's 30-year fixed mortgage rate ticked up to 6.36% (refinance 6.88%) as of July 3 — up from 6.25% last week — putting monthly payments at ~$2,995 on a median NJ home; U.S. equity markets are closed today for July 4 with the Dow at an all-time record and VTI near multi-month highs.
    Source: NerdWallet

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Livingston's 89th Annual July 4 Features NJ's Largest Auto Show (9am) and Fireworks at 9:15pm
    Livingston's 89th Independence Day celebration opens with NJ's largest annual auto show at 9am, followed by food, music, and family activities, capped by fireworks at 9:15pm — about 12 miles from Montclair and a great day-trip for car and motorsport enthusiasts.
    Source: NJ Family
  • Elizabeth's July 4 Combines America's 250th Birthday Events With World Cup 2026 Fan Zone Watch Party
    Elizabeth's all-day July 4 celebration at Veterans Memorial Waterfront Park blends America's 250th anniversary programming with a 2026 World Cup Fan Zone watch party — live entertainment, food vendors, kids' activities, and fireworks at dusk.
    Source: Elizabeth NJ 250
  • America's 250th: Trenton Opens Old Barracks Museum With Revolutionary War Reenactments; Princeton Morven Museum Hosts Free Festival
    Trenton's Old Barracks Museum reopens today with Revolutionary War reenactments, a multicultural parade, and walking tours; Princeton's Morven Museum hosts a free outdoor festival with music and artmaking — both excellent day trips for curious kids, about 45 minutes from Montclair.
    Source: NJ Family

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Zabit Magomedsharipov Injured Out of ACBJJ 21; Brother Khasan Steps In vs. Raul Rosas Jr.
    Zabit Magomedsharipov's highly anticipated return to competition at All Combat BJJ 21 on July 5 has been called off after he sustained an injury in training; his brother Khasan Magomedsharipov will step in to face Raul Rosas Jr. in his place.
    Source: MMA Mania
  • ADCC Opens Roadshow Hits Croatia Today, Miami July 11; Krakow Worlds Set for Sept 12–13
    The ADCC Opens Roadshow continues with a stop in Croatia today (July 4), followed by Miami on July 11, giving competitors their final chances to qualify for the ADCC World Championships in Krakow, Poland, on September 12–13.
    Source: ADCC Official

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Spain Routs Austria 3–0 in Round of 32; Spain vs. Portugal Showdown July 7
    Spain dominated Austria 3–0 on July 2 to advance in the World Cup Round of 32, with Grimaldo playing the full 90. Spain faces Portugal in a blockbuster clash on July 7.
    Source: NBC News
  • Lee Kang-in to Atlético Madrid Imminent; 5-Year Deal Through 2031 for ~€30M
    PSG midfielder Lee Kang-in is set to join Atlético Madrid on a five-year contract through 2031 for a transfer fee of approximately €30 million, with both clubs finalizing paperwork this week.
    Source: Star News Korea
  • Grimaldo: "My First Choice Was Always Atlético" — New Signing Speaks Out
    Newly signed Atlético left-back Alejandro Grimaldo told reporters "my first choice was always Atlético," dispelling suggestions he was a second option for the club, and warned that the World Cup squad must stay focused heading into the knockout rounds.
    Source: Tribuna.com
  • Laporta: Barcelona Has "Moral Obligation" to Sign Álvarez; Atlético Demands €150M Cash
    Barcelona president Joan Laporta declared his club has a "moral obligation" to sign Julián Álvarez and confirmed a €130M post-World Cup bid; Atlético have rejected it, insisting on €150M in cash with no swap deals.
    Source: Football Transfers

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Dow Hits All-Time High +595 Pts on Weak June Jobs Report; Markets Closed Today for July 4
    The Dow surged 595 points to a record on July 2 after June's jobs report came in at 57,000 — well below the 113,000 expected — boosting rate-cut hopes. US markets are closed July 3 for the Independence Day holiday.
    Source: TheStreet
  • AAPL Rebounds 4.8% on AI Plans; Q3 Earnings July 30 With 14–17% Revenue Growth Guidance
    Apple shares rose 4.8% Wednesday, the biggest single-day gain in months, as the company outlined AI integration plans including Google Gemini on iPhones; Q3 earnings are due July 30 with management guiding for 14–17% revenue growth.
    Source: Barchart
  • Spotify Removes 500K Fake Streams After $3M Kalshi Prediction Market Fraud; Asks Platforms to Remove Branding
    Spotify purged over 500,000 streams from Malcolm Todd's "Earrings" and flagged an elaborate $3M prediction-market fraud scheme on Kalshi after traders allegedly manipulated the song's chart position; Spotify has asked Kalshi and Polymarket to remove its branding from their platforms.
    Source: Bloomberg
  • Chip Stocks Sink Despite Dow Record: Micron –7%, SanDisk –14%, AMD –4.3%
    While the Dow hit a fresh record Wednesday, semiconductor stocks bucked the trend with heavy losses — Micron fell 7%, SanDisk dropped 14%, and AMD slid 4.3% — on continued fears of AI-demand softening and supply overhang.
    Source: Yahoo Finance

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Walnut Street Kitchen Closing July 31; Farewell Filipino-American Pop-Up "Bunso" July 7–31
    Montclair's beloved Filipino-American restaurant Walnut Street Kitchen (98 Walnut St.) will close its doors on July 31. Owners are hosting a farewell pop-up series called "Bunso" from July 7–31, serving a special menu for regulars to say goodbye.
    Source: The Montclair Girl
  • Jersey City Council Unanimously Rejects Revised 15% Property Tax Hike; $255M Deficit Unresolved
    Jersey City's council voted unanimously July 1 to reject the mayor's revised 15% property tax increase proposal, following the earlier pulled 20% hike. The city's $255 million structural deficit remains unresolved, and officials warn a lump-sum increase may still follow.
    Source: Gothamist
  • Whitesbog Blueberry Summer Fest Today at Whitesbog Historic Farm, Burlington County
    The Whitesbog Blueberry Summer Festival runs today (July 3) at Whitesbog Historic Farm in Burlington County, featuring live music, local vendors, and family activities — a classic NJ outdoor tradition perfect for the holiday weekend.
    Source: NJ Family

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Helena Crevar vs. Paige Ivette Clymer Set for ONE: The Inner Circle on July 17
    With 15 days to go, ONE Championship confirmed Helena Crevar's return bout against ADCC West Coast Trials winner Paige Ivette Clymer in a 10-minute openweight submission grappling match in Bangkok — one of the most anticipated women's grappling matchups of the summer.
    Source: ONE Championship
  • UFC BJJ 2 Confirmed for July 31: Tackett Defends Title Against Renato Canuto
    UFC's competitive BJJ series returns with its second card on July 31, where champion Tackett will defend his title against submission specialist Renato Canuto as part of an ambitious 14-event UFC BJJ calendar for 2026.
    Source: MMA Mania
  • ADCC 2026 Is 10 Weeks Out With Open Roster Spots After Twin Withdrawals
    ADCC Worlds in Krakow (September 12-13) is now 10 weeks away, but the roster still has openings after Mica Galvao and Giancarlo Bodoni both withdrew — leaving organizers to finalize replacement invites ahead of the stacked Tauron Arena event.
    Source: ADCC Combat

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Spain vs. Austria Kick Off Today at SoFi Stadium in World Cup Round of 32
    Spain face Austria today at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California — kickoff 6pm ET — with Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena and Marcos Llorente both in the squad as Spain look to reach the Round of 16.
    Source: ESPN
  • Lee Kang-in's Atlético Madrid Signing Expected to Be Officially Announced This Week
    Korean media now report the official announcement of Lee Kang-in's move to Atlético Madrid is expected this week, following earlier reports that a €35M fee was agreed and the player signed personal terms through 2031 — a move that would make him the first Asian player ever to represent Atlético.
    Source: Star News Korea
  • Barcelona President Laporta Publicly Addresses Álvarez Deadlock With Atlético
    Joan Laporta stepped in front of cameras for the first time on the Julián Álvarez saga, acknowledging Barcelona's interest while insisting any deal must be done with 'respect for contracts,' as Atlético holds firm at €150M and presses an active FIFA complaint against Barça.
    Source: Football Transfers

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

    Source: BJJ Doc
  • Gracie Barra Wins Team Title at IBJJF American Nationals; Grand Slam Contenders Clay, Hopstock, Jaworski Take Gold Again
    Gracie Barra claimed the overall team title at the IBJJF American Nationals (June 25–27, Las Vegas), while Grand Slam frontrunners Elisabeth Clay, Tarik Hopstock, and Pawel Jaworski all won gold again to stay on course for the No-Gi Grand Slam crown.
    Source: FloGrappling
  • Polaris Announces First-Ever Mainland Europe Events: Open Spain in Barcelona and Open Netherlands in Utrecht
    Polaris is expanding beyond the UK for the first time, debuting Polaris Open Spain in Barcelona on August 29 followed by Polaris Open Netherlands in Utrecht on October 24 — opening the promotion's open-tournament circuit to continental European competitors and fans.
    Source: Polaris Pro Grappling

    Former ADCC silver medalist Jacob Rodriguez is returning to professional grappling competition on July 24 at the Pit Submission Series, ending an absence of more than 17 months since his last match.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Mbappé Brace Destroys Sweden 3-0 at MetLife, Sets All-Time World Cup Knockout Goals Record
    Kylian Mbappé scored in the 45th and 74th minutes and Bradley Barcola added a third as France cruised past Sweden 3-0 at MetLife Stadium on June 30; Mbappé's 6-goal tournament total sets the all-time World Cup knockout stage scoring record and France advance to face Paraguay in the Round of 16.

    Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín formally lodged a FIFA and RFEF complaint accusing Barcelona of illegally approaching Julián Álvarez; separately, Atlético also rejected a €150M bid from Real Madrid for the striker, publicly mocking both clubs, even as Barcelona prepares a revised offer of up to €135–150M.

    Lee Kang-in has agreed personal terms with Atlético Madrid on a contract through 2031 for a fee of approximately €35M, with his PSG exit now confirmed; if completed, he would become the first Asian player ever to represent Atlético.

Financial Freedom & Markets

    The Legendary Count Basie Orchestra under guest conductor John Faddis kicks off the 2026 Montclair Jazz Festival Soundcheck Series tonight at Lackawanna Station — with the Alvin Ailey Dance Company joining in honor of America's 250th — building to the August 15 Downtown Jamboree with Dianne Reeves and Christian McBride.

    As of July 1, Montclair State University's College of Communication and Media assumes management of New Jersey's four public TV stations, returning control to a NJ institution for the first time since 2011 and launching a nightly NJ-centric newscast and at least 6 hours of local programming per week.

    This Saturday's annual Montclair Independence Day celebration features an 11 a.m. parade down Bloomfield Avenue and Valley Road to Edgemont Park, a family picnic, and an evening fireworks show at Yogi Berra Stadium on the Montclair State campus — all free and a short drive from anywhere in town.

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Barcelona's €100M Álvarez Bid Rejected; Clubs Meet as Atlético Privately Concedes Exit Is Near
    Atlético turned down Barcelona's initial €100M bid for Julián Álvarez and are holding firm at €150M, but direct club-to-club meetings are now confirmed; Atlético privately concede the departure is near-inevitable after Simeone reportedly lost patience following the player's public transfer request.

    Paraguay pulled off a massive Round of 32 upset, beating Germany 4–3 on penalties after a 1–1 draw, while Morocco similarly shocked the Netherlands 3–2 in a shootout; France plays Sweden tonight (June 30) at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford at 5pm ET.

    Leon Goretzka's Bayern Munich contract expired June 30, making him a free agent with Atlético Madrid among interested clubs; however, his ~€15M/year salary demands are beyond what Atlético can accommodate, with Sporting's Morten Hjulmand remaining the club's top midfield target.
    Source: TribalFootball

Financial Freedom & Markets

    Apple ended the quarter near $282 with a Buy consensus (avg. target $315); Counterpoint Research forecasts iPhone's global market share rising to 25% and Mac to 12% by year-end, suggesting demand remains resilient despite recent device price hikes driven by memory shortages.

    A free outdoor showing of "Love, Simon" (2018, PG-13) is scheduled for July 1 at 50 South Fullerton Ave in Montclair — a family-friendly pre-holiday film night ideal for tweens and teens.

    Families near Montclair can catch back-to-back World Cup knockout matches at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford: France vs. Sweden tonight (June 30, 5pm ET), Spain vs. Austria on July 2, and Argentina vs. Cape Verde on July 3 — all within a 30-minute drive.

    UFC heavyweight and feared leg-lock specialist Valter Walker says he has dropped jiu-jitsu and wrestling from his training entirely ahead of his July 25 Abu Dhabi bout, opting to trade strikes instead, with one exception if he ever fights Josh Barnett.

    Polaris 32 made history June 28 with the promotion's first all-female Squads showdown at Swansea Arena, with Brianna Ste-Marie's back-to-back wins sealing a narrow 5-4 win for North America after Nia Blackman stepped in as a late-replacement captain for Ffion Davies.

    Atlético and PSG are closing in on a deal for Lee Kang-in worth roughly €30-35M, with PSG now arranging personal terms with Monaco's Maghnes Akliouche as his direct replacement, a clear sign the transfer fee is largely settled.

    Atlético are preparing a roughly €25M bid for Udinese centre-back Oumar Solet, jumping ahead of Inter Milan, whose lower offer has stalled while the Serie A club waits on outgoing sales to fund the move.

    Alphabet (GOOGL) replaced Verizon in the Dow Jones Industrial Average effective June 29, joining Nvidia, Amazon, Apple and Microsoft and pushing the price-weighted index's tilt further toward AI and cloud computing.
    Source: CNBC

    Brent crude rose about 0.9% Monday after weekend US-Iran strikes renewed doubts about a return to normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, even as both sides agreed to resume ceasefire talks in Doha.
    Source: Al Jazeera
  • NJ Homeowners Insurance Premiums Climbed 7.5% Last Year, Outpacing Pennsylvania
    New Jersey home insurance rates rose 7.5% over the past year versus just 1% in Pennsylvania, driven by more frequent severe weather and rising labor and materials costs, though NJ's average premium ($1,449) still trails the $2,395 national average.

    The MC Hotel on Bloomfield Avenue has become an unofficial World Cup basecamp, with Germany's team spotted there and England fans waiting over an hour for their team's bus to arrive as squads use Montclair as a stopover for matches at MetLife Stadium.

    Yellow Rose Vegan Bakery & Cafe, the all-vegan, kosher bakery known for its original Maplewood shop, has opened a new outpost inside Lackawanna Plaza at 1 Lackawanna Plaza in Montclair.

    The New Jersey Lottery SpeedTour with SVRA brings F4 U.S. and FR Americas open-wheel racing back to NJ Motorsports Park in Millville July 31-August 2, part of a packed 2026 season that also includes monster trucks.

    With Gordon Ryan's retirement leaving the ADCC superfight belt vacant for the first time in 17 years, Kaynan Duarte will challenge Yuri Simoes for the title at September's World Championship in Krakow, Poland.

    Joslyn Molina has accepted her invite to the -65kg division at ADCC 2026, making her the youngest athlete ever to compete at the prestigious championship after organizers lowered the age-eligibility threshold.

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

    Álvarez told ESPN he has informed Atlético's hierarchy of his desire for a transfer, with Barcelona his preferred destination; Atleti's CEO is refusing to sell and has threatened a FIFA complaint against Barcelona over an alleged improper approach.

    Atlético and PSG midfielder Lee Kang-in have reportedly agreed personal terms, but Juventus has emerged as a late complication as the clubs negotiate a transfer fee nearing €35 million.

    The FIFA World Cup's Round of 32 kicks off today with South Africa facing Canada at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, the first of a full week of knockout-stage matches across the tournament.
    Source: NBC Sports

Financial Freedom & Markets

    Apple is seeking U.S. government clearance to source DRAM from sanctioned chipmaker CXMT as a severe AI-driven memory shortage drives up component costs, though the move risks the same bipartisan backlash that sank a similar 2022 effort.

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

    King Charles III toured Roger Gracie Academy's London headquarters and was awarded a white belt by Roger Gracie himself, in a visit spotlighting Reorg, a military and emergency-responder charity that uses jiu-jitsu in veterans' recovery; the King also presented a black belt to a Reorg trustee who credits the sport with helping him through cancer treatment.
    Source: Jits Magazine

    Just days after announcing B-Team's revival, Craig Jones gave a blunt interview admitting to long-term steroid use — including injecting before EBI in Tijuana — and said he considers it cheating but stays open about it because 'the next generation is gonna take it anyway.'
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

    Britain's Owen Jones avenged a three-year-old loss to Fabricio 'Hokage' Andrey, edging him on the scorecards after a tense leg-lock battle to win the night's lone grappling bout and snap Andrey's three-fight win streak in ONE Championship.
    Source: ONE Championship

    With ADCC Worlds set for September in Krakow, organizers quietly removed their official invite and qualification list from the website without explanation, leaving fans to piece together the lineup from athlete announcements and fueling debate over contested invites like Josh Saunders' return.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Álex Baena's Strike Sends Spain Top of Group, Knocks Out Uruguay
    Atlético midfielder Álex Baena scored the only goal in the 42nd minute as Spain beat Uruguay 1-0 in Guadalajara, topping Group H and eliminating Uruguay from the World Cup while Cape Verde also advanced to the Round of 32.
    Source: ESPN

    Atlético have agreed personal terms with Stuttgart's Enzo Millot and plan to trigger his €23 million release clause, with Simeone targeting the playmaker — who scored 12 goals last season — as the club's eighth summer signing.
    Source: TribalFootball
  • Dembélé Hat Trick Powers France Past Norway 4-1 as Sørloth Watches From the Bench
    Ousmane Dembélé scored three first-half goals as France routed Norway 4-1 at the World Cup; Norway rested Atlético's Alexander Sørloth and Erling Haaland but still advanced to the Round of 32 as Group I runner-up.
    Source: ESPN

  • Nasdaq Logs Fifth Straight Losing Session as Tech Selloff Caps Worst Week in Months
    The Nasdaq fell for a fifth consecutive session Friday — down roughly 5% on the week — as Sandisk and Micron led chip-stock losses on AI-spending jitters and a report that OpenAI may delay its IPO, even as SpaceX shares rose ahead of a fast-tracked Russell 1000 addition.

    AAPL closed up 3.14% at $283.78 Friday, clawing back part of Thursday's price-hike-driven selloff, even as the company's Vision Pro hardware chief left for OpenAI; Morgan Stanley kept a Buy rating and $360 price target.
    Source: The Motley Fool

    Source: Simply Wall St

    PSE&G has automatically enrolled residential customers in a new Time-of-Use plan charging about $0.31/kWh during weekday 4-9pm peak hours versus roughly $0.09/kWh off-peak, with a 12-month savings guarantee for households that shift laundry and EV charging to nights and weekends.

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Montclair's 4th of July Parade & Fireworks Returns to Yogi Berra Stadium
    Montclair's annual Independence Day celebration kicks off with an 11am parade down Bloomfield Avenue and Valley Road to Edgemont Park, followed by a family picnic and an evening fireworks show at Yogi Berra Stadium on the Montclair State campus.
    Source: Township of Montclair
  • New Eats Land on Bloomfield & Church: Toastique, Hummus Republic Open, Ani Ramen Adds Sushi
    Montclair's dining scene keeps expanding with Toastique opening a gourmet-toast cafe on Church Street, Hummus Republic taking over a former convenience store on Bloomfield Avenue, and Ani Ramen launching a new sushi program at its Bloomfield Ave location.
    Source: The Montclair Girl

    New Jersey Motorsports Park's 2026 schedule adds a Vintage Racer Group weekend of classic cars on track July 10-12 in Millville, ahead of the New Jersey Lottery SpeedTour with SVRA bringing F4 and Formula Americas racing July 31-August 2.

item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Ben Eddy Survives Illegal Slam DQ in ADCC Dallas-Fort Worth Open Absolute
    Ben Eddy, who took bronze at -70kg with four submission wins, was slammed by blue belt Jakori Savage during overtime of the absolute division at the ADCC Dallas-Fort Worth Open, drawing a disqualification; Eddy said he escaped without serious injury.
    Source: Jits Magazine
  • Islam Makhachev Reveals He's Turning Down Grappling and Wrestling Super-Fight Offers
    UFC lightweight champion Islam Makhachev says he has received offers to compete in standalone grappling and wrestling super-fights but is declining them, citing camp demands and injury risk outside his MMA schedule.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe
  • Former WWE Star Tom Pestock Wins Gold at Jiu-Jitsu World League Event
    Tom Pestock, known to wrestling fans as Baron Corbin, added another medal to his growing competitive BJJ resume with a gold-medal finish at a Jiu-Jitsu World League tournament.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Atlético Madrid Officially Completes Grimaldo Signing From Leverkusen
    Atlético confirmed Alejandro Grimaldo as a new player on a deal through 2029 (plus an optional fourth year) for a fixed €15M fee plus variables, with the left-back saying he's 'always liked Atlético' ahead of his move to the Metropolitano.
    Source: Esto es Atleti
  • USMNT Stunned by Turkey in Stoppage Time but Still Tops World Cup Group
    The United States lost 3-2 to Turkey at SoFi Stadium on a last-gasp Kaan Ayhan goal in a dead-rubber match, having already clinched first place in Group D and a Round of 32 date with Bosnia and Herzegovina.
    Source: CBS News
  • Atlético's Sørloth and Norway Face Mbappé's France for Group I Top Spot
    Fresh off a brace against Senegal, Atlético striker Alexander Sørloth lines up with Norway against France on June 26 in Foxborough with first place in Group I on the line ahead of the World Cup Round of 32.
    Source: Al Jazeera
  • Juventus Push to Seal Sørloth Exit From Atlético Amid Nico González Swap Talk
    Juventus and Alexander Sørloth's camp have personal terms agreed on a contract through 2029, but Juventus and Atlético are still negotiating a fee (Atlético want around €35M, Juve nearer €30M), with a possible Nico González swap also on the table.
    Source: Into the Calderon

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Tech Selloff Deepens on Report OpenAI May Delay IPO to 2027
    Asian and U.S. tech stocks fell to a two-week low after a report said OpenAI may push its IPO into 2027, sending SoftBank shares down as much as 13% and reviving fears about AI-spending payoffs even as fresh data showed the U.S. economy growing faster than estimated.
    Source: Bloomberg
  • Apple Shares Extend Slide as UBS Flags 19% Drop in China iPhone Sell-In
    AAPL fell another ~6% to $275.42 after UBS data showed iPhone sell-in in China dropped 19% year-over-year in May, deepening worries that Apple's recent price hikes on Macs and iPads could trigger demand destruction; Wall Street's average target of $314 still implies upside.
    Source: TipRanks
  • Spotify Shares Tick Up on New Ticketing Feature Ahead of July 28 Earnings
    SPOT rose about 2.7% in a recent session, even as the stock remains down roughly 19% year-to-date, as investors eye the rollout of 'Reserved,' a Premium ticketing feature built with Live Nation and Ticketmaster, with 34 of 41 covering analysts rating it buy/outperform.
    Source: TIKR
  • Jersey City Pulls Proposed 20% Property Tax Hike From Vote After Backlash
    Facing a $255 million budget deficit, Jersey City's mayor yanked a proposed 20% property tax increase from the June 24 council agenda after public outcry; a new vote is set for July 1, with the average $11,000 tax bill potentially rising nearly $2,000 if it proceeds.
    Source: PIX11

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Montclair Library Lands $36.6M State Grant for Major Overhaul
    The Montclair Public Library was awarded $36.6 million in NJEDA tax credits for a four-year renovation of its Main and Bellevue Avenue branches, including a new youth-focused floor with a STEAM lab, podcasting studio, and sensory room.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • Vintage Motorcycle Racing Roars Into NJ Motorsports Park This Weekend
    The 14th annual AHRMA Vintage Motorcycle Festival runs June 26-28 at NJ Motorsports Park in Millville, featuring vintage road and sidecar racing on Thunderbolt Raceway plus a swap meet, go-karting, and family-friendly activities.
    Source: New Jersey Motorsports Park
  • Montclair High School Sends Off Class of 2026
    Montclair High School held its Class of 2026 graduation ceremony on June 25 at the school's outdoor amphitheater, with Principal Jeffrey Freeman telling graduates resilience matters as much as their diplomas.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • Free 'Summer of Soccer' World Cup Watch Parties Continue at Lackawanna Station
    Montclair's Lackawanna Station is hosting a 39-day 'Summer of Soccer' series through July 19, screening World Cup matches on big screens alongside youth clinics, food vendors, and tournament play for the whole family.
    Source: Patch (Montclair, NJ)

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Craig Jones Announces Return of B-Team Jiu-Jitsu With New Academy
    Nearly a year after his dramatic exit from the original B-Team, Craig Jones announced he is reviving the B-Team brand with a brand-new academy that will serve as the team's headquarters, though the location has not yet been revealed.
    Source: BJJ Eastern Europe
  • Kade Ruotolo Withdraws From ONE Championship Title Defense Due to Injury
    Ruotolo pulled out of his scheduled ONE Lightweight Submission Grappling World Title defense against Fabricio Andrey after sustaining an injury in his recent MMA win; Andrey has instead been rebooked against newcomer Owen Jones at ONE Fight Night 44 in Bangkok.
    Source: ONE Championship
  • Eight Athletes Qualify for ADCC 2026 Worlds at Asia & Oceania Trials in Gold Coast
    Roberto Frias scored one of the trials' biggest upsets by beating favorite Lucas Kanard to win the -88kg title, while Kaya Rudolph, Bekzat Kapashov, and women's qualifiers Nadia Frankland and Matilda Reid also punched their tickets to ADCC Worlds in Krakow.
    Source: FloGrappling
  • Bia Mesquita Extends Unbeaten UFC Run With Third Straight Submission Win
    BJJ legend Beatriz "Bia" Mesquita stayed undefeated in the UFC, submitting Melissa Mullins with a first-round armbar at UFC Vegas 119 after surviving an early scare, and immediately called out Ailin Perez for a future matchup.
    Source: MMA Mania

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Atlético and Leverkusen Reach Full Club-to-Club Agreement on Grimaldo, Beyond Personal Terms
    Atlético Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen have closed a club-to-club deal for left-back Alejandro Grimaldo in the €20-25M range, with the player signing through 2029 plus an option — multiple outlets now call it done pending his medical and official presentation once Spain's World Cup run ends.
    Source: El Desmarque
  • Atlético to File Formal FIFA Complaint Against Barcelona Over Álvarez Tampering
    Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín announced the club will lodge a complaint with FIFA accusing Barcelona of negotiating with Julián Álvarez — under contract until 2030 — during the protected period, escalating the saga from rhetoric into formal regulatory action.
    Source: ESPN
  • Correction: Bernardo Silva Signed With Real Madrid, Not Atlético, on a Free Transfer
    Real Madrid officially confirmed Bernardo Silva on a free transfer after his Manchester City exit, signing a two-year deal under Mourinho — closing the door on Atlético's reported pursuit and contradicting the prior report that they were leading the chase.
    Source: ESPN
  • World Cup 2026: Group Stage Winding Down, Knockouts Begin Sunday
    The 2026 World Cup has passed its midpoint with Argentina (Álvarez, Messi) already through after beating Austria 2-0, while Spain — with Grimaldo on the squad — face Uruguay Friday in their final group match ahead of the Round of 32 starting June 28.
    Source: ESPN

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Market Rally Extends Into Thursday on Micron Follow-Through; Dow Hits Intraday Record
    The S&P 500 and Dow extended Wednesday's Micron-driven rally into Thursday, with the Dow touching a fresh intraday record of 52,655.66, while the Nasdaq's gains were capped at a more modest 0.24% as Apple's slide weighed on the index.
    Source: Bloomberg
  • Apple Drops ~5-6% After Hiking Mac, iPad, and Vision Pro Prices to Offset Memory Shortage
    Apple raised prices by up to $300 across Mac, iPad, Vision Pro, and HomePod (e.g., MacBook Air to $1,299) citing a DRAM/NAND shortage tied to AI data-center demand, sending shares down 5-6% intraday; UBS kept a Neutral rating with a $296 target and Apple hinted further hikes may follow this fall.
    Source: Bloomberg
  • VTI Hits Fresh High as Vanguard Overtakes iShares as Largest ETF Provider
    VTI traded around $364.64 Thursday, riding the broader Micron-fueled rally, while Vanguard has reportedly overtaken iShares to become the largest ETF provider overall — a notable shift for index investors who rely on funds like VTI.
    Source: TipRanks

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • New Japanese Restaurant Ju-Ichi Opens on Bloomfield Ave as Uncle Momo Closes After 15 Years
    Ju-Ichi, a family-owned ramen and sushi spot with locations in PA and Morristown, has opened its fourth location at 512 Bloomfield Avenue, while longtime Lebanese/Mediterranean spot Uncle Momo is closing this month after 15 years due to an unsustainable rent increase.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • New Italian Restaurant Clementina Opens in Upper Montclair
    Clementina, a modern Italian restaurant from Chef Michele Rocchi, opened June 5 at 627 Valley Road in the former Saunders Hardware space, adding to Montclair's deep bench of Italian spots.
    Source: Montclair Local
  • Montclair Jazz Festival Announces 2026 Lineup Headlined by Dianne Reeves and Christian McBride
    The 17th annual Montclair Jazz Festival's all-day Downtown Jamboree + Block Party is set for Saturday, August 15 at Lackawanna Plaza, featuring Dianne Reeves, Christian McBride Big Band with Bilal, and a youth-focused second stage from JAZZ HOUSE KiDS.

    Montclair State University was selected over a competing independent public-media proposal to manage New Jersey's four FCC-licensed public TV stations, taking over programming and operations on July 1.
